title: Some Sing Of His Power-who Has That
subtitle: Jap · Ang 1
summary: Control is carried here from some sing of His Power-who has that Power? toward o Nanak, He blossoms forth, Carefree and Untroubled.
whyItMatters: This shabad is useful when life feels gripping, controlling, tense, because it keeps control inside remembrance, conduct, and the Creator's larger care instead of private mood.
takeaway: Control steadies when o Nanak, He blossoms forth, Carefree and Untroubled.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗਾਵੈ ਕੋ ਤਾਣੁ ਹੋਵੈ ਕਿਸੈ ਤਾਣੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: gaavai ko taan hovai kisai taan ||
lines.translation: Some sing of His Power-who has that Power?
Some sing of His Gifts, and know His Sign and Insignia.
Some sing of His Glorious Virtues, Greatness and Beauty.
Some sing of knowledge obtained of Him, through difficult philosophical studies.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗਾਵੈ ਕੋ ਸਾਜਿ ਕਰੇ ਤਨੁ ਖੇਹ ॥
lines.transliteration: gaavai ko saaj kare tan kheh ||
lines.translation: Some sing that He fashions the body, and then again reduces it to dust.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗਾਵੈ ਕੋ ਜੀਅ ਲੈ ਫਿਰਿ ਦੇਹ ॥
lines.transliteration: gaavai ko jeea lai fir dheh ||
lines.translation: Some sing that He takes life away, and then again restores it.
Some sing that He seems so very far away.
Some sing that He watches over us, face to face, ever-present.
There is no shortage of those who preach and teach.

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਥਿ ਕਥਿ ਕਥੀ ਕੋਟੀ ਕੋਟਿ ਕੋਟਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: kath kath kathee koTee koT koT ||
lines.translation: Millions upon millions offer millions of sermons and stories.
The Great Giver keeps on giving, while those who receive grow weary of receiving.
The Commander, by His Command, leads us to walk on the Path.
O Nanak, He blossoms forth, Carefree and Untroubled. ||3||

structure: The opening movement names the pressure directly: some sing of His Power-who has that Power?.
The middle movement deepens the correction by holding the mind inside some sing that He watches over us, face to face, ever-present.
The closing movement leaves a return you can actually keep: o Nanak, He blossoms forth, Carefree and Untroubled.
